module_title: Advanced Analysis - Structural Reforms, IBC, and Bad Banks
introduction: This advanced level analyzes the macroeconomic impact of India's massive NPA crisis and the aggressive, structural legal reforms introduced by the Government and the RBI to recover bad loans and clean up bank balance sheets.

core_concepts.title: Twin Balance Sheet Problem
core_concepts.description: A term popularized by former Chief Economic Advisor Arvind Subramanian. It refers to a dual crisis: 1. Indian 'Corporates' had over-leveraged (borrowed too much) and their balance sheets were ruined. 2. Simultaneously, the 'Banks' that lent them money had their balance sheets ruined by the resulting NPAs. Both were trapped together.

core_concepts.title: SARFAESI Act, 2002
core_concepts.description: (Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act). This powerful law allows banks to seize, auction, and sell 'collateral' (pledged assets like factories or houses) of defaulting borrowers 'without' requiring the intervention of a court. (Note: It does not apply to agricultural land).

core_concepts.title: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC, 2016)
core_concepts.description: A game-changing legal framework. It established a strictly time-bound process to resolve corporate bankruptcies. If a defaulting company cannot come up with a viable restructuring plan within 330 days, the company is forcibly liquidated (sold off in pieces) to pay back the banks.

core_concepts.title: Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) Framework
core_concepts.description: This is the RBI's 'Intensive Care Unit' for weak banks. If a bank's NPAs rise too high or its capital drops too low, the RBI places it under PCA. The bank is immediately slapped with severe restrictions: it cannot issue new big loans, cannot open new branches, and cannot distribute dividends to shareholders.

important_entities.name: Bad Bank (NARCL)
important_entities.description: A 'Bad Bank' (officially the National Asset Reconstruction Company Ltd. in India) is a unique entity that does NOT accept deposits or give out loans. Its sole purpose is to 'buy' the massive, toxic NPAs from commercial banks (at a discount) and attempt to recover the money. This instantly cleans up the commercial banks' balance sheets, allowing them to resume lending.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In statement-based questions, examiners often write: 'A Bad Bank is a bank that provides high-risk loans to poor citizens.' This is a TRAP. A Bad Bank is simply an Asset Reconstruction Company (ARC). It does not interact with the general public or provide loans.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: 1. Recognize (identify NPAs honestly). 2. Recapitalize (infuse fresh capital into weak banks). 3. Resolve (use IBC/SARFAESI to recover money). 4. Reform (change banking laws to prevent future crises).

exam_strategy_tips: Knowing the exact year of the SARFAESI Act (2002) and the IBC (2016) is absolutely mandatory for matching questions.
